messages.subject_clean: Is the bioconductor version the latest?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

Yes, you are right this is a bug. I opened an issue on our GitHub (https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/issues/280), but do currently not have the time to work on this.

To get this working you may use run this code prior to calling the function, which is essentially the fix that I will upload soon:

```
setMethod("getCorrelation", "methylBaseDB",
          function(object,method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"),plot,nrow=2e6){

            if(is.null(nrow)){

              meth.fun <- function(data, numCs.index, numTs.index){

                data[, numCs.index]/( data[,numCs.index] + data[,numTs.index] )
              }
              meth.mat = methylKit:::applyTbxByChunk(object@dbpath,return.type = "data.frame",
                                         FUN = meth.fun, numCs.index = obj...@numCs.index,
                                         numTs.index = obj...@numTs.index)
            }else{
              data = methylKit:::headTabix(object@dbpath,nrow=nrow,return.type = "data.frame")
              meth.mat = data[, obj...@numCs.index]/( data[,obj...@numCs.index] +
                                                        data[,obj...@numTs.index] )
            }

            names(meth.mat)=obj...@sample.ids

            method <- match.arg(method)
            print( cor(meth.mat,method=method) )

            if(plot) {
              methylKit:::.plotCorrelation(meth.mat = meth.mat,
                               title = paste(object@context, object@resolution ,method,"cor."),
                               method = method)
            }
          }
)
```

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: sd.filter not available with unite?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

The sd filtering options have been implemented in the visualization functions since they speed up computations and remove features that do not or only minimally contribute to the final outcome. We can safely keep them as default without influencing the outcome too much.

That being said before we could do any filtering on regions we have to use the unite function to merge samples based on common regions.
But I don't see any reason not to filter the regions for low variance after uniting, since people also do this for differential expression testing.

Concerning you rother question, there is currently no way to return the filtered object used by the clustering function, but you may check out the code in our repo to see how the filtering is done internally:
https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/blob/4735b6fca820c8bda1f84b03e12d19bada2df1fc/R/clusterSamples.R#L290-L307

Since we can simply select regions of interest,  a simple workflow to filter regions could look like this:

```
pm <- percMethylation(mdb)
sds=matrixStats::rowSds(as.matrix(pm))
cutoff=quantile(sds,0.5)
filter=which(sds>cutoff)

mdb_lowVar <- mdb[filter]
```

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Vector restrictions for treatment?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

Will a numeric vector of numbers other than 1 and 0 cause problems? Say a vector of 1 and 2 for case and control?

No, using different numbers works as long as you use two distinct numbers for case and control. When you run `calculateDiffMeth` it will actually print a message telling you which number it choose as case/treatment and control. By default, the lower number will be chosen to represent the control group, which will be the second term of the methylation subtraction. This is important to consider when later interpreting the results in terms of hyper/hypo methylation.

You can test which data types work using the internal test data:

```
library(methylKit)

data("methylKit")

methylRawList.obj |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth() #works
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(c(2,2,3,3)) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth() #works
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(as.factor(c("a","a","b","b"))) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth() #works, but not officially supported
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(c("a","a","b","b")) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth() #fails
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(as.character(c(2,2,3,3))) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth() # fails
```

Will a factor be interpreted correctly or should we always explicitly give a vector of 1 and 0s?

Factors will be internally converted to numerics, so they work but should be taken with a grain of salt.
```
factor(x = c(3,3,2,2),levels = c(3,2)) |> as.numeric()
factor(x = c(3,3,2,2),levels = c(2,3)) |> as.numeric()
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(factor(x = c(3,3,2,2),levels = c(3,2))) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth()
methylRawList.obj |> `getTreatment<-`(factor(x = c(3,3,2,2),levels = c(2,3))) |> unite() |> calculateDiffMeth()
```
This being said it should be favoured to be explicit with the treatment vector and use numerics directly.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: assembly and annotation bed file
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The assembly variable for methylKit is just there for bookkeeping,  we are not using it internally, so you do not have to do anything special here.
Concerning the gene annotation bed file, you can perform all the steps of the normal comparative analysis without the need for the annotation file.

If UCSC supports your organism, the BED file can be obtained from the table browser (https://genome-euro.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTables).
If you have a gtf/gff instead of a bed file there is some untested code to use these instead of the BED file (https://github.com/BIMSBbioinfo/genomation/issues/192).

Best,
Alex

Hi Muktesh,

We can only filter for contexts when using methRead with bismarkCytosineReport. However, you would still need to load the complete files into memory, thus I think your approach to use a single report file per context is already fine.
The Bismark coverage file does not have any context information, so again, you have to provide separate files for each context to use this.

I do actually not understand what “duplicate” issue you are talking about, but maybe what you are seeing is that after using methRead you keep fewer CpG sites than expected. This might happen since we are applying a default coverage filter of minimum 10 reads (argument ‘mincov'), to remove uninformative CpG sites.

I hope this helps.

Best,
Alex

Dr Muktesh Chandra <drmuk...@gmail.com> schrieb am Mi., 19. Apr. 2023, 20:05:
Hi Alex,

Thank you for your reply.

I reached out to a few internet resources, I used Bismark.coverage from Bismark extractor into methylkit. I want to use CHH, CHG content also, so, how do I define them in methread function, as bismark.cov report does not have any context information (if I use context = CHH/CHG, in methread() input does not have that information). Therefore, I used another method, by using --CX report and CpG/CHH/CHG context report, and made a methylkit supported format for all three context separately. But when I used this converted file issue come up in memory, to resolve it I did remove the duplicates and it worked fine for me (consulted thread "https://github.com/al2na/methylKit/issues/63").

But further getting deep into CpG context 28Million Cs were there before duplicate removal, but after removal, I only got 7M, is it correct I am losing 3/4th of the Cs?. Second I was wondering where the duplicate arise when we ran the deduplication step to remove PCR duplicates, in bismark.

I still want to figure out what would be the correct approach to have an analysis done from all three (CpG/CHH, CHG context).

I will appreciate your suggestion

Thank you
_
Muktesh

On Wed, Apr 19, 2023 at 10:48 AM Alexander Blume <alex....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Muktesh,

The awk command on the cytosine report returns all the lines for a given context independent of the methylation context, so there is no linear relationship between %C methylation and the number of lines per context.

Concerning your other question, I can say that for mammalian genomes the number of non-CpG-sites is way higher than CpG sites, so your ordering of CHH>CHG>CpG makes sense.

Best,
Alex

drmuk...@gmail.com schrieb am Donnerstag, 13. April 2023 um 22:06:20 UTC+2:
Hi,

I am analyzing plant WGBS, I ran bismark, and % of C methylated were maximum in CpG > CHG >CHH context. I used awk '($6=="CG")' filename.CX.report.txt to get CpG context report and similarly I did for CHG and CHH context. My question is on counting the lines in each context order was CHH>CHG>CpG; is it normal?.
As having high %C methylated in CpG context, number of lines should be higher in CpG context. Any suggestions

I will appreciate your suggestions or explanations.

Thank you

-
Muktesh

messages.body_plain:
Hi Muktesh,
it is normal because number of CHH sites are far more than that of CHG and CG sites irrespective of methylation status. Therefore, overall number of mCs will be higher in CHH sites depending on plant species. In contrast, the proportion of mCs within the context will be highest in CG followed by CHG and CHH contexts. Hope you are cleared.
